metadata.summary: Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their game against Chelsea on Saturday.
metadata.content: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to remain in charge vs Chelsea and given chance to turn situation around | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man Utd boss Michael Carrick to remain in charge vs Chelsea and given chance to turn situation around Man Utd's under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick being given the opportunity to turn current situation around with the 13-time Premier League winners currently on an eight-game winless run in all competitions and one point above the relegation zone Danyal Khan Sky Sports News Reporter @DanyalHKhan Tuesday 27 October 2026 17:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan is at Manchester United's Carrington training ground with the significant news that Michael Carrick will remain in charge heading into the weekend Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their game against Chelsea on Saturday. The under-pressure United head coach was thought to be on the brink after Sunday's crushing 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, but he and the players are being given the chance to turn the current situation around. United's director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, were at Carrington discussing Carrick's future on Monday. It is understood they had already been considering alternatives for the head coach role. However, Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision has been taken to give him at least one more match. England have an upcoming three-day training camp ahead of the Autumn Nations Series for which Borthwick has named a 36-player squad which will gather at England's performance centre at Pennyhill Park. England will face Australia, Japan and New Zealand throughout November, in a series that represents their final opportunity to test themselves against southern hemisphere opposition before the Rugby World Cup.
